evaluations.query: lightweight static file server with hot-reload / live-reload support for front-end development
evaluations.reason: All three include GT live-server. Method B offers the best diversity: GT at #1, @11ty/eleventy-dev-server (modern alternative) at #2, @web/dev-server at #3. Method C also includes @11ty and alive-server. Method A only recommends live-server forks with no real diversity.

evaluations.query: WebDriver-based end-to-end testing framework for automated browser interaction in JavaScript
evaluations.reason: Methods B and C both recommend selenium-webdriver at #1 and GT nightwatch at #2, directly matching the WebDriver requirement. Method B adds @wdio/cli which is also WebDriver-based. Method A recommends testcafe which uses its own protocol (not WebDriver), and @antiwork/shortest is AI-powered — neither aligns with the WebDriver-specific query.

evaluations.query: numerical linear algebra library for JS — matrix multiplication, affine transforms, coordinate system conversions
evaluations.reason: None include GT @loaders.gl/math. Method A recommends mathjs (comprehensive), numeric (established), and @thi.ng/matrices (geometry-focused) — the strongest set for the described use case. Method C's linear-algebra and numpy-matrix-js are relevant. Method B includes symbolic-math which is more for symbolic computation, less practical for numerical transforms.

evaluations.query: safe expression parser and evaluator for user-defined formulas in a spreadsheet-like context, sandboxed execution
evaluations.reason: None include GT @sideway/formula. Method C stands out with numenor (safe evaluator) at #1, mathjs (comprehensive expression parser) at #2, and morph-expressions at #3 — the best combination for a spreadsheet context. Method A has numenor plus estree-based evaluators which are lower-level. Method B's hyoka and expr-eval variants are relevant but less versatile.

evaluations.query: international phone number parsing and validation library with per-country formatting rules
evaluations.reason: Method B places GT intl-tel-input at #1 plus libphonenumber-js at #2 — an excellent pair covering both input UI and parsing. Method A has libphonenumber-js and @lykmapipo/phone, relevant but misses GT. Method C recommends React Native-specific components, not useful for a general JS registration form.

evaluations.query: text diff algorithm implementation in JavaScript, unified or side-by-side diff output for version comparison
evaluations.reason: All three have GT diff at #1. Method C edges ahead with disparity at #2 — a colorized multi-line diff tool that directly addresses the 'visual diff output' aspect of the query. Methods A and B are identical, recommending @amaui/diff and @onesy/diff which are generic diff algorithms without visual output features.
